[DAY4 17:26:00 - DAY4 17:26:28]

[DAY4 18:01:01 - DAY4 18:01:30]

[DAY4 20:39:30 - DAY4 20:40:00]

I see Nicous knocking on the door. "Playing games," I say. I'm still chatting with them. "I guess he's using earphones," I say. Nicous: "Okay, okay, we need to gather in a bit, okay." I go over to take a look and glance at them.

[DAY4 21:44:30 - DAY4 21:44:58]
I listen quietly as he plays guitar and sings really well. He keeps writing lyrics and pauses briefly; I watch him try other tracks on his phone. Katrina: "Let's start with this." Katrina: "Everyone can sing along." I'm really happy.

[DAY4 21:43:01 - DAY4 21:43:29]
I watch someone shrug — their shoulders relax and their body language shows it. Shure says, "The band from that corner of Sailor Park." When everyone looks up at me, innocent smiles appear. "If it's not in English, you can't tell," I say. Shure laughs, "Haha, indeed, haha." I double over laughing, clutching my stomach and scratching my left arm. I cross my arms and continue to enjoy the music. Katrina asks, "Can this be played with a guitar?" Shure replies, "Should be able to," then stops playing the guitar and searches for music on the tablet. Everyone waits quietly; time seems to stand still.

I begin by moving to the side of the table, picking up the power bank, and unplugging the data cable. I hand the power bank to Tasha, who connects the cable and plugs it into my glasses. She then puts the power bank in her pocket and takes out her phone, while I open a box, grab another data cable, and head outside to the yard where friends are relaxing under an umbrella. I place the data cable on the table and return inside.

I search the bedroom thoroughly, feeling along the bed but do not find the item. Returning to the living room, I pick up the power bank from the power strip and unplug it again. Holding the power bank, I move toward the door as Tasha enters and chats with me. I look around, point to the kitchen, and Tasha locates the item there. I then head outside holding the power bank.

Outside, I walk through the entrance into the yard under the umbrella, where Shure and Nicous are on their phones and Katrina is chatting with them. I instruct, “You need to plug it in. You need to turn it on.” I then turn back into the house, ascend the stairs, pass through the entrance hall, and re-enter the living room where Alice and Tasha are seated at the table; Tasha grabs a bag of snacks.

Carrying a charger, I go into the bedroom, place it on the table, touch my nose, and cross my arms. I pick up the power bank again and return outside. Alice pulls out a chair, and I sit holding the power bank before walking to the yard and standing under the umbrella. Nicous remains on his phone; Shure picks up a phone from the table and stands, while Katrina adjusts her glasses, tidies her belongings, and picks up her bag.

While slowly walking around the yard with the power bank, I look at it and ask, “What’s this?” Tasha answers, “Mint leaves.” I repeat, “Mint leaves,” noting their presence. I engage in brief conversation with the group, look around the yard, and clap my hands as I turn around in the relaxed setting.

I then walk into the room, turn toward the eaves, and cross my arms as Shure comes out carrying a guitar, placing his phone on the table. I follow him to the edge of the umbrella, watching as he pulls a chair, sits, places the guitar on his lap, and strums with his left hand while navigating his phone with his right. Nearby, Nicous chats with Katrina listening, and I affirm with “Yes.”

I then gave her a strawberry and ate one myself, and we agreed to finish the strawberries secretly. After returning the mango to the box, we decided to share the fruit with others upon their return.

Moving to the living room, I picked up two lunch boxes in preparation to go upstairs. Tasha realized she had forgotten her phone, so I waited for her to retrieve it. We then both proceeded upstairs to the second floor, where I noticed Shure, Tasha, and others discussing singing and lyrics. I set down the food but realized I had forgotten chopsticks. After Tasha pointed this out, I retrieved chopsticks from the kitchen cabinet, wiped my sticky hands, and arranged seating by placing a cushion and tidying the sofa cushions as the group gathered on the floor for discussion.

The group began a singing session with Katrina playing the guitar. Shure introduced performers using playful nicknames and maintained rhythm. I greeted members by name and observed the group’s banter about identities and English names. Tasha prompted song ideas, leading to suggestions of familiar and hometown tunes, including an EMO anthem and an Ed Sheeran song. We all engaged by clapping and singing together, while lighthearted critiques of singing skills and joking claims of “nailing it” highlighted camaraderie despite acknowledged vocal limitations.

Shure proposed a Westlife song but admitted he could not play it; Katrina took over guitar duties, asserting her proficiency. I stayed engaged by swaying to the music and drinking quietly. Katrina suggested photographing the moment as Shure played while Tasha and I exchanged attentive glances. The session concluded with everyone immersed in the collaborative musical atmosphere.

During the music selection, I listened to Stefanie Sun’s “First Day” and sang along with Tasha. Katrina and Shure discussed the song’s associations, while I checked WeChat and sent a message before turning off my phone to observe the singing. We discussed the song’s origin and agreed to forgo guitar accompaniment to focus on group singing. The conversation transitioned smoothly as Shure and Katrina noted the event’s timing.

Back upstairs, I initiated questions about singing plans, clarifying that it was a singing event rather than dancing. The group decided to perform two songs—an energetic opener and a relaxed evening piece—and discussed instrument use and visual concepts, concluding collaborative planning with shared laughter.

Responding to requests for power banks, I went downstairs, unplugged multiple devices, and distributed them upstairs to Lucia and Shure, confirming the supply was adequate. After returning downstairs, I fetched and cleaned chopsticks, handing them to Tasha, Katrina, and Shure while noting hygiene concerns from Lucia. I facilitated communal eating by providing chopsticks and engaging with the group’s discussion on mochi flavors and dipping methods, supporting group interaction.

I engaged in a detailed conversation with Lucia, Katrina, and Alice about vaccination schedules and costs, sharing personal anecdotes about animal scratches and vaccinations. Shure intermittently searched for music and suggested listening, which the group accepted, transitioning from health topics to music. I actively participated in song discussions, checked song lists on Katrina’s phone, and facilitated the group’s selection of “Unforgettable Tonight” as the opening number, contributing to performance arrangement discussions including guitar use and introduction placement.

The group addressed musical instrument logistics, confirming the availability of an electric piano owned by Nicous, eliminating the need for rental. We discussed opening performance options and locations, deciding on “New Boy” as the opener and considering “Perfect” by Ed Sheeran for another piece, with discussions about solo dance suitability. I encouraged hesitant members, notably Shure, with lighthearted remarks about conference invitations contingent on participation. The session ended with clear consensus on song choices, participant roles, and collaboration plans.

The group convened to plan and rehearse songs for an upcoming performance. I actively participated by suggesting song choices, confirming familiarity with “Perfect,” and advocating for older songs over new ones. We considered relaxing songs for the second set, with Shure proposing to teach an original band song. After exchanging ideas, I suggested “Song of Grass and Bugs,” leading to a collective decision to focus on Jay Chou’s “Sunny Day” and “Nocturne.” I contributed by tapping rhythms and selecting songs, coordinating with others’ input.

Following song selection, we rehearsed Jay Chou’s pieces in the room. Shure played guitar while I maintained the beat by tapping my hand and fingers. The group practiced together, humming along and solidifying the song choices. The session concluded with Shure affirming the plan to proceed with these songs. We further rehearsed one song under Shure’s guidance, focusing on lyrics and rhythm; I kept the beat as everyone sang, including Nicous and myself at the climax. After the practice, Katrina confirmed the chosen song, and we agreed on the performance.

The group then discussed event arrangement and dinner plans. Shure suggested including a piano solo after dinner, encouraging free combinations of singing and playing. We decided to invite guests who would leave by 8 PM and settled on ordering extra-large Domino’s pizzas for the evening meal. Lucia fetched food while Shure mentioned dipping pizza in a specific sauce as part of the dinner plan.

We finalized the song order and event plans, with me leading the discussion on sequence. We agreed to start with two karaoke-backed songs accompanied by Nicous on guitar, while Shure coordinated via tablet. Planning included a Q&A session for the next day, with reminders to document details and instruct guests to bring second-hand items for auction and exchange. Shure explained the auction process by demonstrating with a bottle of aged white wine from his grandfather, introducing “hook coin” as currency equal to one regular coin, represented on a chain. The group, including Lucia, engaged actively with the lively bidding arrangement.

I reviewed a photo on my phone and confirmed auction and Q&A plans with the group, leading a timeline discussion that set guest arrival between 2:30 and 3:00 PM and emphasized the event’s purpose of fundraising and storytelling. Payment terms were left flexible. We agreed on roles as hosts and judges, seated on small stools. Further logistical planning included Katrina’s suggestion for guest introductions and Shure’s proposal for a warm-up performance to open the event, establishing a clear framework.

The group discussed event activities focusing on games and segments. I confirmed the opening segment before self-introductions and clarified a challenging puzzle game as the “game before party.” We agreed to exclude certain games, opting instead to scatter coins around the venue. I checked coin inventory, initially considering 150 but settling on 20 to manage resources. Katrina reviewed the schedule while I coordinated process details. We planned rewards for puzzle completion, breaking it into sections with incremental incentives supported by Shure, despite playful complaints from others about difficulty and reward size.

The conversation shifted to mining and exploitation metaphors related to the puzzle and reward system. I questioned mining costs while Shure and others discussed, with Lucia clarifying the connection to Bitcoin mining. We maintained focus on balancing game difficulty, rewards, and event flow. The group then explored leveraging blockchain technology, with Lucia suggesting creating NFTs for our work and Alice proposing coin awards based on task time. We clarified related song references, setting a context for using new technologies in our activities.

During a casual interlude, I sat in the living room holding my tablet as Nicous played guitar and Lucia sat nearby. Shure commented on song lyrics sounding censored, and I noted catching one word, highlighting a relaxed moment amid planning.

Katrina outlined the event itinerary as I reviewed it on my devices. The schedule included self-introduction and Q&A from 3:00 to 3:40 PM, hosting segments, another group’s presentation, an auction, pizza ordering, and singing concluding by 8:00 PM. Shure and Katrina confirmed timing with no issues. I noted the evening’s simplicity and confirmed finishing by 8:00.

We addressed logistics for the next day’s barbecue. Katrina asked about leftover charcoal, and I suggested starting grilling tomorrow. Shure agreed to burn charcoal now. The group acknowledged grilling’s challenges, with Lucia and Shure commenting on difficulty. Nicous inquired about my background, to which I responded I was from the northeast, finalizing minor plans.

I led discussion on food preparation, proposing ordering ready-to-eat barbecue skewers for oven warming. Shure supported warming them, while Lucia and Katrina suggested alternatives. The group favored convenient pre-made skewers, also discussing purchasing skewered meat via Meituan and other ingredients, establishing an efficient food plan.

We deliberated on alcoholic drink selection and timing, preferring Vita and including Shure’s proposal for a champagne toast during dinner to add excitement. I agreed and encouraged making it special, concluding drink arrangements with a festive tone.

I reviewed the event itinerary on my phone during group discussion on room decorations and segment placement. I contributed ideas on schedule positioning, and we agreed to schedule a warm-up segment before Q&A from 2:30 to 3:00 PM, ensuring early attendee engagement and organized flow.

Further planning involved explaining game activities in the living room, outlining warming up at 3:00 PM, followed by coin-finding games and purchasing items. Participants, including Tasha, Shure, and Katrina, confirmed understanding, clarifying timing and structure for smooth execution.

I sat with Lucia as Shure paced nearby while finalizing event roles. I accepted responsibility for delivering a general presentation and a brief defense segment to welcome guests and leaders and open the event. Shure humorously questioned my motivation; I affirmed my commitment, establishing key speaking responsibilities to set the event’s tone.

Finally, I searched for my phone and interacted with Shure regarding its whereabouts. After retrieving the phone and returning to the home screen, I glanced at Shure, who said he had found his phone. I then removed my glasses and placed them on the sofa, concluding this interaction.
